body_text:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be open. A twice continuously
differentiable function $u:U\to\mathbb{R}$ is harmonic if it
satisfies Laplace's equation $u_{xx}+u_{yy}=0$ throughout $U$.
If $f=u+iv$ is holomorphic, then both $u$ and $v$ are harmonic.
Locally on a simply connected domain, each harmonic function is
the real part of a holomorphic function, unique up to an
imaginary constant.
